messages:
alex: Noticed multiple support tickets where quotas were charged to the wrong tenant after the SDK 1.4.0 release. Suspect related to the header rename in the client (X-Redwood-Route -> X-Redwood-RouteId).

tara: Oh yikes. We shipped the header rename in 1.4.0 to disambiguate route ids vs human names. But Console routing logic still expects X-Redwood-Route.

ian: That would explain misattribution. Console routing lookup falls back to header if auth mapping absent. If header is missing it picks a default route which points to the org-level bucket.

priya: Can you paste the failing request example?

alex: Example from a support dump: ```http
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
X-Redwood-RouteId: rt_4a2b3c
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "prompt":"foo",
  "max_tokens":64
}
```

priya: Console expects `X-Redwood-Route` and maps route -> tenant using the legacy route-table. New header name means lookup misses and falls back.

tara: So two problems: SDK changed header and Console/ingest are not backwards compatible; and our feature gates/rollout notes weren't clear.

alex: Impact: quota burn shows on org default account for some customers, and per-route latency dashboards are blank. Severity medium but customer-facing.

ian: Immediate remediation options: (1) quick patch in Console to accept both headers (X-Redwood-Route and X-Redwood-RouteId) — low risk; (2) hotfix in SDK rolling back header rename — larger rollback; (3) proxy shim at api edge that copies new header value into legacy header for a rolling window.

priya: I prefer (3) proxy shim — minimal code, instant fix, buy time for proper migration. We can then update Console to accept both headers and mark the old header deprecated in docs.

tara: Agree. Proxy team can add mapping in the edge for a week while console patch lands. Also need to coordinate a deprecation timeline and release notes for the SDK.

alex: I'll open an edge-proxy PR to dup X-Redwood-RouteId -> X-Redwood-Route when present. Template: `if headerExists(Redwood-RouteId) setHeader(Redwood-Route, getHeader(Redwood-RouteId))`.

ian: Console change: accept both headers in route lookup, and add a diagnostic flag in the UI that shows which header was used for mapping. That helps support.

priya: Also add a telemetry event `route.header.missing_legacy` when only new header is present so we can measure adoption. Put in SDK changelog that 1.4.0 uses new header but servers will tolerate both for 30 days.

release-bot: deploy queued: edge/proxy-mappers #778 -> staging at 1718732260 by alex

alex: I'll land the proxy shim now and notify support + account managers. Then open Console PR; I can help with tests.

tara: For longer term, update SDKs (py/ts/go) to accept config toggles: `useLegacyRouteHeader=true|false` so clients can opt in during migration. Also create a docs page "Routing header migration" with code snippets.

ian: Good. Also we should update policy docs: route identifiers accepted in headers must be canonicalized before mapping (strip prefix, lower-case). There was a separate bug where `rt_ABC` didn't match `rt_abc`.

priya: I'll coordinate the communication: support message, release notes, and a short changelog blurb for the SDK releases. Prefer to give customers 7 days notice before removing the shim.

alex: Staging smoke for proxy shim succeeded at 1718732330. Planning prod deploy in 10m.

priya: Thanks. After prod, please watch quota attribution metrics and open a small postmortem if more than 0.1% of tenants still see misattribution.

ian: Filing RFC for canonical header-handling: https://go/repo/rfcs/route-header-canonicalization. Will include tests and e2e for header passthrough across edge, ingest, and console.
